This systematic approach works for all quadratic equations.

To find stationary points: 1) Differentiate f(x) to get f'(x). 2) Set f'(x) = 0 and solve for x values. 3) These x-values are potential stationary points. 4) For each x, find y = f(x). 5) Determine nature using second derivative: if f''(x) > 0, it's a local minimum; if f''(x) < 0, local maximum; if f''(x) = 0, test fails - use first derivative test. 6) Plot points to visualize. Stationary points occur where tangent is horizontal.
